Class ChaosRuntime

java.lang.Object
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.core.ChaosRuntime
All Implemented Interfaces:
ChaosControlPlane, AutoCloseable
@Internal public final class ChaosRuntime extends Object implements ChaosControlPlane
Thin facade that composes ChaosControlPlaneImpl and ChaosDispatcher.

Retained as a single entry point so that existing callers (ChaosBridge, bootstrap, tests) do not need to be updated when the control-plane and dispatch halves are profiled or exercised in isolation. Delegates control-plane methods to ChaosControlPlaneImpl and hot-path methods to ChaosDispatcher.

Not part of the stable API. This class is public only because it is referenced across the chaos-agent internal multi-module split (bootstrap, instrumentation, benchmarks). The frozen public surface is ChaosControlPlane in the api module; bind against that interface instead. The ChaosRuntime-class surface may change without notice in any release. The @Internal marker makes that contract explicit to API linters, IDE inspections, and japicmp-style bytecode tools.

    • activate

      public ChaosActivationHandle activate(ChaosScenario scenario)
      Description copied from interface: ChaosControlPlane
      Activates a single chaos scenario at JVM scope.

      The scenario is validated against selector/effect compatibility and registered immediately. Scenarios with ActivationPolicy.StartMode.AUTOMATIC begin intercepting operations instantly. Manual-start scenarios require a subsequent ChaosActivationHandle.start() call.

      The exceptions have no common root besides RuntimeException: catch the ones below, or RuntimeException. Every failure of an open control plane is recorded once in the diagnostics and published as a FAILED event before it is thrown; an activation on a closed one throws IllegalStateException and records nothing.

      Specified by:
      activate in interface ChaosControlPlane
      Parameters:
      scenario - the scenario to activate; must have ChaosScenario.ScenarioScope.JVM scope
      Returns:
      a handle for lifecycle control; close it to stop the scenario

    • bindSession

      public ChaosSession.ScopeBinding bindSession(@Nullable String sessionId)
      Description copied from interface: ChaosControlPlane
      Binds the calling thread to the open session with sessionId, as ChaosSession.bind() would: how a server joins the session a request came from (ChaosSession.HEADER). The id decides for the binding's lifetime: an unknown or closed id runs the thread outside any session, even one it inherited (a pooled server thread started while a test's session was bound).
      Specified by:
      bindSession in interface ChaosControlPlane
      Parameters:
      sessionId - the session id, e.g. the value of the ChaosSession.HEADER header; null (no header) also runs the thread outside any session
      Returns:
      the binding to close when the work is done

    • validate

      public void validate(ChaosScenario scenario)
      Validates a scenario as activate(ChaosScenario) would, without activating it: nothing is registered, but a refusal is recorded in the diagnostics and published as FAILED, as an activation's is (L21).
      Parameters:
      scenario - the scenario
      Throws:
      ChaosActivationException - if the scenario is session-scoped
      ChaosValidationException - if the scenario is invalid
      ChaosUnsupportedFeatureException - if the runtime cannot run it

    • requireHooks

      public void requireHooks(ChaosScenario scenario)
      Weaves the hooks a scenario needs, as activate(ChaosScenario) would, without activating it: its hook groups, and its method selector added to the ones woven already (a selector whose scenario is never activated is removed at the next removal). A weaving failure is recorded in the diagnostics and published as FAILED.
      Parameters:
      scenario - the scenario
      Throws:
      ChaosInstrumentationException - if its hooks cannot be woven (the weaving failure is the cause)
      ChaosUnsupportedFeatureException - if the runtime cannot weave

    • activate

      public ChaosActivationHandle activate(ChaosPlan plan)
      Description copied from interface: ChaosControlPlane
      Activates all scenarios in a ChaosPlan at JVM scope.

      All scenarios activate atomically: either all succeed or the plan activation fails. The returned handle controls all scenarios in the plan as a group. Every scenario is validated and every hook the plan needs is woven before any scenario is registered.

      The exceptions have no common root besides RuntimeException: catch the ones below, or RuntimeException. Every failure of an open control plane is recorded once in the diagnostics and published as a FAILED event before it is thrown; an activation on a closed one throws IllegalStateException and records nothing.

      Specified by:
      activate in interface ChaosControlPlane
      Parameters:
      plan - all scenarios must have ChaosScenario.ScenarioScope.JVM scope
      Returns:
      a composite handle that stops all plan scenarios when closed

    • openSession

      public ChaosSession openSession(String displayName)
      Description copied from interface: ChaosControlPlane
      Opens a named session scope for per-test chaos isolation.

      Scenarios activated on the returned session affect only threads bound to it: the calling thread, which is bound from this call until ChaosSession.close(), and threads bound with ChaosSession.bind(). Multiple sessions may be active simultaneously without interfering with each other.

      Always close the session when the test completes to stop all session scenarios and release the session scope: 

      try (ChaosSession session = controlPlane.openSession("my-test")) {
    session.activate(scenario);
    // ...
}
      Specified by:
      openSession in interface ChaosControlPlane
      Parameters:
      displayName - human-readable name for this session; appears in diagnostics and logs
      Returns:
      a new session; caller is responsible for closing it

    • addEventListener

      public void addEventListener(ChaosEventListener listener)
      Description copied from interface: ChaosControlPlane
      Registers a listener that receives all chaos lifecycle and application events.

      Listeners are invoked synchronously on the thread that triggers the event. Implementations must be non-blocking and must not throw.

      Common use cases:

      • JFR integration — emit JFR events correlated with chaos activity (built in, installed automatically when jdk.jfr is available)
      • Test assertions — verify that specific scenarios fired during a test run
      • Custom metrics — bridge chaos events to Micrometer, Prometheus, or similar
      Specified by:
      addEventListener in interface ChaosControlPlane
      Parameters:
      listener - a non-null, non-blocking listener; must not throw from onEvent

    • removeEventListener

      public boolean removeEventListener(ChaosEventListener listener)
      Description copied from interface: ChaosControlPlane
      Removes a listener registered with ChaosControlPlane.addEventListener(ChaosEventListener); a listener registered more than once is removed once. Removing an asynchronous listener stops its delivery thread; events still queued for it are discarded.
      Specified by:

    • markJvmWide

      @Internal public void markJvmWide()
      Marks this runtime as the one the agent installed for the whole JVM (ChaosPlatform): its close() is refused from then on, since every caller of ChaosPlatform.installLocally() and current(), the management endpoints and the plan file poller share it. Called by the bootstrap when it publishes the runtime.

    • close

      public void close()
      Stops and removes every scenario, those of open sessions included, cleans up stressor resources and closes the listeners that are AutoCloseable.

      After this call the control plane is inert; all selector evaluations return no-match. An open session stays open but activates nothing more (its activate fails with IllegalStateException); its own ChaosSession.close() still ends its binding of the thread that opened it. Calling close() more than once is safe.

      The JVM-wide control plane the agent installed (ChaosPlatform.installLocally(), current()) cannot be closed: other tests, framework integrations and the management endpoints share it.

      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
      Specified by:
      close in interface ChaosControlPlane
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if this is the JVM-wide runtime the agent installed (ChaosPlatform.installLocally(), current()): stop or close the handles and sessions instead, or activate through a TrackingChaosControlPlane (chaos-agent-testkit) and call its stopTracked()

    • beforeMethodEnter

      public void beforeMethodEnter(String className, String methodName) throws Throwable
      Public hook for OperationType.METHOD_ENTER. Call this from the application's interception machinery (Spring AOP @Around, AspectJ, Micronaut / Quarkus interceptors, or your own bytecode advice) at the start of every intercepted method to give chaos scenarios a chance to inject an exception before the body runs.

      For use without the agent (a plain ChaosRuntime in a unit test). With the agent attached, a MethodSelector scenario weaves its methods itself; calling this hook for them as well evaluates each call twice. A matching MethodSelector scenario with ChaosEffect.ExceptionInjectionEffect causes this method to throw the configured exception type. 

      @Around("@annotation(com.example.Audited)")
public Object intercept(ProceedingJoinPoint pjp) throws Throwable {
  chaosRuntime.beforeMethodEnter(
      pjp.getTarget().getClass().getName(),
      pjp.getSignature().getName());
  return pjp.proceed();
}
      Parameters:
      className - the fully-qualified binary class name of the method's declaring class
      methodName - the simple method name (no descriptor)
      Throws:
      Throwable - the exception type configured by an active ExceptionInjectionEffect; no-op if no scenario matches

    • afterMethodExit

      public @Nullable Object afterMethodExit(String className, String methodName, @Nullable Class<?> returnType, Object actualValue) throws Throwable
      Public hook for OperationType.METHOD_EXIT. Call this from the same interception machinery as beforeMethodEnter(String, String) after the intercepted method body returns; pass the original return value and receive the (possibly-corrupted) value to hand back to the caller.

      A matching MethodSelector scenario with ChaosEffect.ReturnValueCorruptionEffect replaces actualValue with a boundary, null, zero, or empty value selected for returnType. 

      Object result = pjp.proceed();
return chaosRuntime.afterMethodExit(
    cls, mth,
    ((MethodSignature) pjp.getSignature()).getReturnType(),
    result);
      Parameters:
      className - the fully-qualified binary class name of the method's declaring class
      methodName - the simple method name (no descriptor)
      returnType - the declared return type; used to select an appropriate corrupted value (null for reference types, 0 for numeric primitives, false for booleans, empty collections / arrays / strings)
      actualValue - the original return value; primitives must be boxed
      Returns:
      the (possibly-corrupted) value to return to the caller; equals actualValue when no scenario matches
      Throws:
      Throwable - the exception of an active RejectEffect scenario on METHOD_EXIT, thrown after the method body ran (ExceptionInjectionEffect is valid on METHOD_ENTER only)

    • adjustClockMillis

      public long adjustClockMillis(long realMillis)
      Public hook for OperationType.SYSTEM_CLOCK_MILLIS. Pass a raw System.currentTimeMillis() reading and receive the chaos-skewed value to use downstream.

      The agent cannot auto-instrument System.currentTimeMillis() (it is native @IntrinsicCandidate and the JIT replaces calls with a direct hardware-clock read). Application code typically wires this hook into a TimeProvider / Clock wrapper: 

      public long now() {
  return chaosRuntime.adjustClockMillis(System.currentTimeMillis());
}
      Parameters:
      realMillis - real wall-clock time in milliseconds, typically obtained from System.currentTimeMillis()
      Returns:
      chaos-skewed milliseconds when an active SYSTEM_CLOCK_MILLIS scenario applies; realMillis unchanged otherwise

    • adjustClockNanos

      public long adjustClockNanos(long realNanos)
      Public hook for OperationType.SYSTEM_CLOCK_NANOS. Pass a raw System.nanoTime() reading and receive the chaos-skewed value. See adjustClockMillis(long) for the broader context — the same JVM constraint (native intrinsic) applies to nanoTime().

      A backward DRIFT skew on this hook intentionally violates the monotonicity contract of nanoTime() to expose timing-loop and profiling assumptions.

      Parameters:
      realNanos - real monotonic time in nanoseconds, typically obtained from System.nanoTime()
      Returns:
      chaos-skewed nanoseconds when an active SYSTEM_CLOCK_NANOS scenario applies; realNanos unchanged otherwise
